chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris told us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa'id, from Jamil, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding a man who bequeaths a part of his property, the part is one of ten.
Because Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, says: 'Then place upon each mountain of them, a part.'
And the mountains were ten and the birds were four, so He placed on each mountain of them, a part.
ai.seo_question: What is the specific legal definition of 'a part' (al-juz) in Islamic inheritance bequests according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the term 'a part' (al-juz') in bequests specifically denotes one-tenth, deriving this from the Quranic narrative of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) building ten mosques on ten mountains (Quran 2:260). This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on linguistic precision in legal terminology, linking the numerical structure of the verse to the fixed fraction of inheritance. The ruling underscores the principle that specific Quranic contexts can establish definitive legal precedents for general terms in fiqh.
